column1: # TITLE: Selective Requirement for Mediator MED23 in Ras-active Lung Cancer
# SUMMARY: K-RAS activating mutations occur frequently in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)
column2: leading to aberrant activation of Ras-MAPK signaling pathway that contributes to the malignant phenotype. However
column3: the development of Ras-targeted therapeutics remains challenging. Here
column5: a component of the multisubunit Mediator complex that is known to integrate signaling and gene activities
column6: is selectively important for Ras-active lung cancer. By screening a large panel of human lung cancer cell lines with or without a Ras mutation
column7: we found that Med23 RNAi specifically inhibits the proliferation and tumorigenicity of lung cancer cells with hyperactive Ras activity. Med23-deficiency in fibroblasts selectively inhibited the oncogenic transformation induced by Ras but not by c-Myc. Transcription factor ELK1
column8: which is phosphorylated by MAPK for relaying the Ras signaling to MED23
column9: was also required for the Ras-driven oncogenesis. Transcriptiome analysis revealed that MED23 and ELK1 co-regulate a common set of target genes enriched in regulating cell cycle and proliferation to support the Ras-dependency. Furthermore
column10: correlated with the strength of Ras signaling as indicated by the ELK1 phosphorylation level
column12: and was found to be overexpressed in both Ras-mutated lung cancer cell lines and primary tumor samples. Remarkably
column13: lower Med23 expression predicts better survival in Ras-active lung cancer patients and xenograft mice. Collectively
column14: our findings demonstrate a critical role for MED23 in enabling the “Ras-addiction” of lung carcinogenesis
column15: thus providing a vulnerable target for the treatment of Ras-active lung cancer. To gain a genome-wide understanding of how MED23 and ELK1 control gene expression in Ras-active lung cancer cells
